in_arabic.name: جيش
in_arabic.meaning: جيش يعني الجيش أو القوة العسكرية
in_arabic.long_meaning: جيش هو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ج-ي-ش' والذي يعني التجمع أو الجمع. يشير الاسم إلى فكرة القوة والجماعة, ويعبر عن معاني مثل الجيش أو الفوج. في اللغة العربية, الاسم يستخدم للدلالة على القوة العسكرية أو الجماعة المنظمة. كما ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنفال آية 11 'وَلَقَدْ أَرَسلْنَا مَلَائِكَتَنَا مَعَ أَثَقيلٍ وَأَنزَلْنَا الْقُرْآنَ وَمَا كُنا لِذَليلٍ'

in_urdu.name: جیش
in_urdu.meaning: جیش کا مطلب فوج یا قوت ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: جیش ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے فوج یا قوت. یہ نام عربی جذر 'ج-ي-ش' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے اکٹھا کرنا یا جمع کرنا. یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے اور اس کا مطلب فوجی قوت یا طاقت کے طور پر سمجھا جاتا ہے. اردو میں, جیش کا استعمال فوج یا مسلح افواج کے حوالے سے کیا جاتا ہے.

in_hindi.name: जैश
in_hindi.meaning: जैश का अर्थ है सेना या शक्ति
in_hindi.long_meaning: जैश एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है सेना या शक्ति. यह नाम अरबी मूल 'ज-य-श' से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ है एकत्र करना या इकट्ठा करना. भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, जैश का उपयोग सेना या सैन्य बल के संदर्भ में किया जाता है. यह नाम शक्ति और साहस के प्रतीक के रूप में भी प्रयोग किया जाता है.

in_pashto.name: جيش
in_pashto.meaning: جيش د فوج یا پوځ معنی دی
in_pashto.long_meaning: جيش د عربي نوم دی چې د فوج یا پوځ معنی لري. دا نوم د عربي ريښو 'ج-ي-ش' څخه اخيستل شوی دی چې د راغونډولو يا ټولګې معنی لري. په پښتني او افغان کلتور کې، جیش د نظامي ځواک یا پوځ د يو سمبول په توګه کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Jaish
in_english.meaning: Jaish means army or military force
in_english.long_meaning: Jaish is an Arabic name derived from the root 'j-y-sh' meaning to gather or collect. It refers to a group of people, particularly an army or military force. In Islamic tradition, the name Jaish symbolizes strength, unity, and collective power. The name has been used historically in various Muslim cultures to signify a strong and organized group.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jaish has significant cultural importance for Muslims, as it is associated with the concept of Jihad, which is a fundamental religious and moral obligation for every capable Muslim. Jaish evokes images of brave warriors or armies fighting to protect their lands, beliefs, and communities against oppression, tyranny, and injustice. Historically, many Islamic armies and military movements were given this name to reflect their commitment to defend Islam and their people. Today, the term is used to represent various Islamic political and military groups seeking to establish Islamic rule or defend Muslim interests.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jaish holds special significance as it underscores the Islamic principle of struggle and self-sacrifice in seeking the pleasure of Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is reported to have said, "Jihad is the way to repel the enemy and secure Allah's pleasure." The name Jaish is thus a reminder of the importance of striving for the sake of Allah and the immense spiritual rewards that come from it. By carrying this name, an individual is encouraged to be a righteous and committed servant of Allah who is willing to fight for the cause of truth and justice.

historical_references.reference: Jaish al-Muhajirin wa'l-Ansar (Army of Emigrants and Helpers), also known as Jaish Muhammad (Army of Muhammad), was a major military expedition led by the Prophet Muhammad (570-632 CE) in 624 CE against the Banu Qurayzah tribe. It was one of the first major military campaigns of Islam and marked the end of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The name 'Jaish' means 'army' in Arabic.

Jaish al-Islam (Army of Islam) is a Sunni Islamic militant group in Syria, founded in 2011 during the Syrian Civil War. It is known for its strict Salafist ideology and has been designated as a terrorist organization by various countries and organizations, including the United States. The name 'Jaish' reflects the group's belief in establishing an Islamic state in Syria.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Jaish' is an Arabic word meaning 'army' or 'military force'. In modern context, it is commonly used to refer to militant groups in the Middle East, particularly those associated with terrorism. Some well-known groups bearing this name include Jaish al-Fatah, Jaish al-Islam, and Jaish al-Adl. Jaish al-Fatah, for example, is a coalition of Sunni Muslim rebel groups in Syria that has been designated as a terrorist organization by several countries. Jaish al-Islam is another radical Islamist militant group, primarily active in Iraq, known for its brutal tactics and extreme interpretation of Islamic law. Jaish al-Adl is an armed militant group based in Iran, primarily active in the southeastern provinces of Iran and Pakistan, known for its attacks on security forces and civilians. Jaish groups have been known to use social media extensively to recruit members, spread propaganda, and coordinate attacks. News media frequently covers their activities, both in the regions where they operate and globally. Military operations against these groups are a common feature in contemporary Middle Eastern conflicts.
